styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Yellow Crane Tower, Hubei Museum and the riverside.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hot dry noodles, street breakfasts and night markets.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: 1911 Revolution sites and the old three towns.

stays.why: Historic concession streets, big malls and easy metro links; good base for food and nightlife.
Closest to Yellow Crane Tower, the Hubei Museum and East Lake; handy for Wuchang station.
Quieter and cheaper; good for Guiyuan Temple and ferry hops across the Yangtze.
Modern area near East Lake and universities; suits tech-minded travelers and longer stays.

food: Start the day like a local: hot dry noodles (reganmian), a sesame-paste noodle dish, usually ¥5–10 a bowl.
Try doupi (sticky rice and egg pancake) and mianwo rice cakes at breakfast stalls; cheap and filling.
Snack streets: Hubu Alley near Yellow Crane Tower and Jiqing Street in Hankou for evening food.
Wuhan food is spicy and river-based; ask for less chili (bu la) if you need it.
Street stalls are cheapest; sit-down restaurants run about ¥40–100 per person. Check hygiene with your eyes.
more_time: Add a day for East Lake: rent a bike and ride the greenway; allow 3–4 hours.
Take the ferry across the Yangtze for a cheap river crossing and skyline views.
Day trip to Guiyuan Temple in Hanyang for a quieter half-day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the tower, the museum and a food crawl across the three towns without rushing.

month_notes: Cold and damp: highs near 9°C, lows around 2°C. Pack a warm coat.
Still chilly, highs about 12°C; rain on roughly 10 days.
Milder spring, highs near 18°C; good for walking.
Warm and wetter, highs near 27°C; carry an umbrella.
Hot and rainy: highs around 30°C, rain on about 15 days.
Very hot, highs near 32°C; plan indoor sights midday.
Hottest month, highs around 33°C; go out early or late.
Still warm at 30°C but drier; a good shoulder month.
Comfortable autumn, highs near 23°C; great for East Lake.
Cold again, highs near 11°C; fewest rain days at about 6.

climate_guide.summary: Humid subtropical: hot, wet summers and cool, damp winters. Spring and autumn are the best times to visit.

items.title: Best time: April to May and September to October
items.text: Highs around 23–30°C with manageable rain. Ideal for walking and the lake.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (June to August)
items.text: Highs of 30–33°C and lows near 26°C. Muggy nights; plan indoor sights at midday.

items.title: Rain peaks in June
items.text: About 15 rain days in June. Keep a compact umbrella and a backup indoor plan.

items.title: Cool, damp winter
items.text: January highs near 9°C and lows around 2°C. Buildings can feel cold; bring warm layers.

items.title: Rain most months
items.text: Expect 6–15 rain days any month. Showers are often short, so carry rain gear rather than cancel plans.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes and sun protection for summer; a warm coat for winter; an umbrella year-round.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; ferries for river views and short hops.

modes.text: 12 lines and 300+ stations. Line 2 links the airport and Hankou station; Line 4 links Wuhan and Wuchang stations. Fares are distance-based; a Wuhan Tong card costs ¥15 and gives about 10% off.
Flat fare ¥1–2 (¥0.8–1.6 with card). Alipay and WeChat QR codes work on many routes.
Metered and cheap. DiDi works well; Uber does not operate in China.
Not needed for a city visit; metro and taxis cover the sights.
Good for short hops and riverside walks; shared bikes help between nearby spots.
Ferries cross the Yangtze between the three towns; a cheap way to see the river.
Two streetcar systems serve Hanyang and the Guanggu area.
